title: A Letter for the Regiment
premise: In the winter of 1918, Rosalind Nystrom, an apprentice clockmaker in the garrison city of Vellmark, is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock—the instrument that regulates every regimental schedule in the city. There she meets Elias Brandt, a deserter from her own father's old regiment who carries letters in handwriting identical to that of Captain Aldous Nystrom, officially dead for three years. As armistice negotiations stall and the military governor tightens his grip on the city, Rosalind discovers her father faked his death to expose a supply-corruption ring reaching into the governor's own office. Racing to finish the clock before the governor can seize the observatory and destroy the evidence hidden inside its mechanism, Rosalind must choose between loyalty to the institution that raised her and the truth her father died—nearly—to tell. The book ends with the armistice signed at dawn, the clock striking true for the first time in months, and Rosalind publicly claiming both her name and her father's unfinished work.
about_author: B. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring mechanical clocks in northern Europe before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about ordinary craftspeople caught in the machinery of history.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Summoned to the observatory, she diagnoses the master clock's failure—a worn escapement no one else can name—and feels the quiet pride of a craftsperson history never notices. Beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Service Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Elias Brandt appears at the workshop after hours, soaked and desperate, carrying letters she recognizes as her dead father's hand. He claims Captain Nystrom is alive. She throws him out. Beat: the past breaching a sealed door.

chapters.title: What the Governor Wants
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias evades a patrol and reflects on deserting: he was ordered to burn regimental ledgers proving stolen supplies. He needs the clock tower because the captain hid copies there. Beat: fear sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Handwriting
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Comparing the letters against her father's old workshop notes, she cannot deny the match. Grief curdles into anger—if he lived, why let her mourn? Beat: betrayal before belief.

chapters.title: The Observatory at Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. Rosalind returns to repair the clock by lamplight; Elias waits among the gears. They strike an uneasy bargain: she repairs, he searches, neither trusts the other. Beat: alliance born of necessity.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Inside the clock's base casing Elias finds a hollow lined with oilcloth—but empty except for a key stamped with the regiment's crest. Someone got here first. Beat: hope deferred.

chapters.title: The Governor's Clockmaker
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Governor Halvard summons her, courteous and chilling, offering a commission to refit the observatory 'for security.' She realizes he wants the clock under his control before the armistice. Beat: power smiling with its teeth showing.

chapters.title: Apprentice No Longer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her master, old Soren, reveals he knew her father's suspicions and chose silence to protect the shop. Rosalind sees how survival becomes complicity. Beat: disillusionment with a mentor.

chapters.title: The Crest Key
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias traces the key to a decommissioned regimental chapel being converted to a munitions depot. A near-capture costs him his papers. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Mainspring
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Working against a deadline imposed by the governor's men, she rebuilds the mainspring and finds a second hiding place in the fusee cone—this one holding half a ledger page naming a quartermaster. Beat: proof at last, but partial.

chapters.title: The Quartermaster's Daughter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The named quartermaster turns out to be the father of her closest friend Marta. Confronting Marta risks everything; saying nothing makes her complicit. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: Arrest Warrant
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Soldiers raid the workshop looking for 'a deserter.' Soren covers for Elias and pays with his arrest. Rosalind watches the shop she loves become a crime scene. Beat: the cost of sheltering truth.

chapters.title: Negotiations
chapters.summary: Governor Halvard's POV (first use). Armistice talks stall; Halvard plans to declare martial law and blame 'sabotage' at the observatory, giving him pretext to hold power past any peace. Beat: the antagonist's cold arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Chapel Vault
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Rosalind and Elias break into the chapel at night and recover the full ledgers from beneath the altar floor. Pursued, they escape across frozen marshland. Beat: triumph shadowed by exhaustion.

chapters.title: What My Father Built
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Reading the ledgers, she learns her father hid them inside a clock he designed himself—the very master clock she has been repairing. His message was addressed to whoever could read the mechanism. It was always meant for her. Beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Governor Halvard's POV. Halvard's men plant evidence of sabotage in the observatory and set the seizure in motion for dawn. He orders the clock stopped permanently. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Stopped
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Arriving to find soldiers dismantling the clock, Rosalind bargains with the officer in charge using her guild credentials, buying one night alone with the mechanism—an offer Halvard, needing a working clock for his ceremony, grudgingly accepts. Beat: audacity as last resort.

chapters.title: One Night of Work
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Rosalind restores the clock while Elias copies the ledgers for distribution to delegates arriving for the signing. A soldier nearly catches them; Marta arrives, having chosen truth over family, and holds the door. Beat: all debts called in.

chapters.title: The Strike of Six
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. At the armistice ceremony, the master clock strikes six and its chime sequence triggers a hidden compartment releasing the ledger copies above the assembled officers and delegates. Halvard's men move to seize Rosalind; Elias steps forward and surrenders himself to give the documents time to spread through the crowd. Beat: sacrifice and exposure.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Delegates halt the signing until the corruption is investigated; Halvard is taken into custody by his own allies to save the peace. Rosalind testifies, naming names including her friend's father. Beat: justice that still hurts.

chapters.title: The Living
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In a prison infirmary she finally meets her father—old, broken, alive. Their reunion is not forgiveness but beginning: he asks what she built, and she tells him. Beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Keeping Time
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue. Spring. The observatory clock keeps perfect time; Rosalind holds her journeyman's certificate, earned in her own name. Elias, pardoned, tends the workshop garden. History, she understands now, happens to everyone—it is only ever repaired by someone willing to open the case. Beat: quiet, earned resolution.
